== Rycar Ryjerd framing ==
* Bill's view (26 October 2026): "He's an idiot" on [[Rycar's Run]] is Decipher joking about the smuggler [[Rycar Ryjerd]], not about his namesake. The same goes for "the terminally insane" on [[They'd Be Crazy To Follow Us]].
* His reasons: [[Jerry Darcy]] was a Decipher employee through 1999, designed sets after Dagobah, including Special Edition, and came up with the idea for Objectives. A jab at him in print is very unlikely.
* Both entries on [[Jokes]] and both card pages now say the lore mocks Rycar, and mention Darcy only as the source of the anagram. No other entry reads as mocking a real person. [[User:Comlink Cursor|Comlink Cursor]] ([[User talk:Comlink Cursor|talk]]) [[User:Comlink Cursor|Comlink Cursor]] ([[User talk:Comlink Cursor|talk]]) 11:38, 26 October 2026 (UTC)
* Follow-up (26 October 2026): Bill asked for the anagram mention to be dropped. The [[Rycar's Run]] and [[They'd Be Crazy To Follow Us]] entries on [[Jokes]], and both card pages, no longer name [[Jerry Darcy]]; they say only that the lore calls Rycar an idiot as a joke. [[Anagrams]] is unchanged. [[User:Comlink Cursor|Comlink Cursor]] ([[User talk:Comlink Cursor|talk]]) 13:57, 26 October 2026 (UTC)

== Effective Repairs: the one-hand reading ==
Bill decided this entry on 26 October 2026, after rewatching the scene. The card's picture is from the short scene early in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' where the ''Millennium Falcon'' flees Hoth under attack and Han works on the damaged hyperdrive motivator with one hand.<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> That scene comes before Luke lands on Dagobah, and long before Luke loses his hand at Cloud City. [[Dagobah Limited]] (April 1997) also came out before [[Cloud City Limited]] (November 1997).<ref name="expansions">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Star Wars CCG: The Expansions], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990504174938/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Internet Archive], 4 May 1999.</ref> So the lore is not about Luke's hand or [[Bionic Hand]]. It turns the idiom "take matters into his own hands" into "his own hand" for a one-handed repair. The [[Jokes#Effective Repairs|Jokes]] row and the [[Effective Repairs]] card page now say this, and the entry was removed from [[User:Comlink Cursor/Jokes candidates]]. [[User:Comlink Cursor|Comlink Cursor]] ([[User talk:Comlink Cursor|talk]]) 16:01, 26 October 2026 (UTC)

== Prepare The Chamber and Slayn & Korpil Facilities: sources checked ==

'''[[Prepare The Chamber]]''': Bill asked whether the card refers to laughing gas or drugs.
* The lore says the TCF32's coolant "is rumored to have a mildly euphoric effect on Ugnaughts" and that "Individuals on TCF32 duty are regarded with envy". It does not name a gas or a drug.<ref name="dec-ptc">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/cloudcity/dark/large/preparethechamber.html Prepare The Chamber], Decipher card list (card image). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010124125500/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/cloudcity/dark/large/preparethechamber.html Internet Archive], 24 January 2001.</ref> The art shows the carbon-freezing pit filled with white vapour.
* The title matches a stage direction in the script, "Six Ugnaughts frantically prepare the chamber for use." In the script's dialogue Vader says "Reset the chamber for Skywalker"; nobody says "prepare the chamber".<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref>
* Wookieepedia's article on the TCF32 cites only this card. No Wayback copy could be made of it (Save Page Now returned 520), so it is not linked here.
* The Usenet groups rec.games.trading-cards.misc and rec.arts.sf.starwars.games were searched in full.<ref name="usenet-rec">[https://archive.org/details/usenet-rec Usenet rec.* archive] (mbox files for rec.games.trading-cards.misc and rec.arts.sf.starwars.games), Internet Archive.</ref> The card appears in about 125 posts, all about decks, rules or trades. No post mentions the coolant, euphoria, gas or drugs.
* Saved copies of DeckTech posts and of Decipher's website have no design comment on this lore.
* Reading (not sourced): the joke is that the work fumes give the workers a mild high, so the job everyone envies is the one next to the freezing pit. Nothing found says the intended reference is laughing gas or any particular drug. The [[Jokes#Prepare The Chamber|row]] was changed only to restate the lore exactly ("a job the Ugnaughts compete for" and "make them happy" were looser than the card) and to add the matching script stage direction. The joke line on [[Prepare The Chamber]] was changed to the same wording.

'''[[Slayn & Korpil Facilities]]''': looking for a real "that means quality" slogan.
* No real advertisement or slogan of the form "X owned, and that means quality" was found. The search covered the web, the same Usenet archives (the one "means quality" hit is an unrelated post about Decipher), and West End Games' ''Strike Force: Shantipole'', which introduced the Verpine, Roche and the B-wing project and has no such line.
* The closest real copy found, neither shown to be the source: the Old Spice jingle line "Old Spice means quality!"<ref name="ads-l-oldspice">[https://listserv.linguistlist.org/pipermail/ads-l/2018-August/152427.html 21st-Century Advertising Slogans], American Dialect Society mailing list (ADS-L), 9 August 2018 (recalls the Old Spice jingle). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027124528/https://listserv.linguistlist.org/pipermail/ads-l/2018-August/152427.html Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref> and a 1952 department-store ad for Alligator coats, "It's Alligator, of course, and that means quality".<ref name="statesman-1952">[https://oregonnews.uoregon.edu/lccn/sn85042470/1952-10-10/ed-1/seq-4/ocr/ ''The Oregon Statesman'' (Salem), 10 October 1952, page 4] (text), Historic Oregon Newspapers. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027124604/https://oregonnews.uoregon.edu/lccn/sn85042470/1952-10-10/ed-1/seq-4/ocr/ Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref>
* The [[Jokes#Slayn & Korpil Facilities|row]] is unchanged and no image was added: no slogan source was found, and neither ad above is an image from an SWCCG site. [[User:Comlink Cursor|Comlink Cursor]] ([[User talk:Comlink Cursor|talk]]) 12:48, 27 October 2026 (UTC)
* Follow-up, Bill's call (27 October 2026): both ad lines now go in the [[Jokes#Slayn & Korpil Facilities|row]] and in the joke line on [[Slayn & Korpil Facilities]], as real ads in the same form as the lore and not as its proven source. The Old Spice line also cites Neatorama, which dates the jingle ("The Old Spice Sea Shanty") to 1953.<ref name="neatorama-jingles">[https://www.neatorama.com/2015/02/20/Jingle-Fever-the-Stories-Behind-Ad-Jingles/ Jingle Fever: The Stories Behind 5 Ad Jingles], Neatorama (20 February 2015). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027131154/https://www.neatorama.com/2015/02/20/Jingle-Fever-the-Stories-Behind-Ad-Jingles/ Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref> The row shows [[:File:Joke reference - Alligator coat ad, Oregon Statesman 1952.jpg]], cropped from the newspaper's page scan; Save Page Now returned 520 for the page scan and PDF, so the file page cites the preserved text page of the same newspaper page. No Old Spice image was added: the two 1950s and 1960s Old Spice commercials on the Internet Archive (1957 and 1965) do not use the jingle, and no archived print ad carrying the line was found. [[User:Comlink Cursor|Comlink Cursor]] ([[User talk:Comlink Cursor|talk]]) 13:16, 27 October 2026 (UTC)
* Second follow-up, at Bill's request (27 October 2026): an Internet Archive full-text search for "and that means quality" found about 30 advertisements using the form, from Hart Schaffner & Marx (1906) to Trane (1987). Others include Paris Garters (1930s and 1940s), Kiwi polish (1941), Jeep (1974), Owens-Corning shingles (1979), Bates saddlebags (1980) and Goodyear Eagle tires (1981). The row and the card page now quote the three closest in shape and date to the card: Buick Regal (1976, "Regal is a Buick. And that means quality."), Toyota Corolla (1983, "Each Corolla is a Toyota. And that means quality famous the world over.") and Trane (1987, "it's made by Trane. And that means quality."). None of them is claimed as the source of the joke. The Alligator image is now a close-up of the quality line, because the whole ad was too small to read in the row. Save Page Now refused the three Internet Archive item pages (error 523), so those refs link the Internet Archive items directly. No image of the Old Spice jingle was found. [[User:Comlink Cursor|Comlink Cursor]] ([[User talk:Comlink Cursor|talk]]) 13:35, 27 October 2026 (UTC)
* Bill's call (27 October 2026): the Wayback Machine excludes archive.org's own pages, so the Buick (1976), Toyota (1983) and Trane (1987) refs link the Internet Archive scans directly, with no Preserved copy. [[User:Comlink Cursor|Comlink Cursor]] ([[User talk:Comlink Cursor|talk]]) 14:21, 27 October 2026 (UTC)

== Food and being fat (27 October 2026) ==

This section was Bill's call (27 October 2026, relayed by Chief): a new Running gag on food and being fat. The block is [[Jokes#Food and being fat|Food and being fat]], and the type table now counts 9 running gags and 164 jokes.

'''Included.''' [[Cloud City: Dining Room]] (Dark Side card; its Light Side text doubles Blue Milk, Beru Stew and Yoda Stew and makes "Jek" deploy -2) with [[Jek Porkins]] (Light Side), shown side by side; the three food cards [[Blue Milk]], [[Beru Stew]] and [[Yoda Stew]]; [[Max Rebo]]; [[WHAAAAAAAAAOOOOW!]]; [[Oh, Switch Off]]. Each card page has a matching <code>joke=</code> line. The game text and lore are quoted from the wiki card pages and agree with swccg-card-json.

'''Ortolan: cross-linked, not moved.''' The page lists a multi-category joke once, under one type, and points to it from the other blocks: [[Jokes#Figrin D'an's band|Figrin D'an's band]] sends readers to [[Tedn Dahai]] in Union jokes, and [[Jokes#I have a bad feeling about this|I have a bad feeling about this]] points to Main Course. Alpha1's [[Jokes#Ortolan|Ortolan]] row is a design gag (the game text pays off the lore), so it stays under Design gags, and the new block's opening paragraph links to it. [[Max Rebo]], the Ortolan who signs up for unlimited food, has his own entry in the new block. The opening paragraph also links the food jokes already listed under other types: Frozen Dinner, Main Course, and Chewbacca Of Kashyyyk and Always Thinking With Your Stomach.

'''Data to check.''' The Ortolan row says the Dining Room is "a site in Jabba's Palace". The only Decipher card with that name is [[Cloud City: Dining Room]], a Cloud City site; there is no Jabba's Palace Dining Room. That row was left as it is for its author to check.

'''Build notes.''' New Decipher.com archive faces, taken from Wayback copies of Decipher's card list GIFs: [[:File:CC-D-cloudcitydiningroom-decipher-archive.gif]], [[:File:JP-L-maxrebo-decipher-archive.gif]] and [[:File:Dagobah-L-whaaaaaaaaaoooow-decipher-archive.gif]]. Decipher's Yoda Stew GIF has no Wayback copy, so the block uses the existing [[:File:Dagobah-L-yodastew.gif]]. Hootkins' remark about the name Porkins is cited to SlashFilm (4 December 2023), and the film lines to the IMSDb scripts; each citation has a checked Internet Archive copy. No film stills were added, because the card pictures already show each scene.

== Vader choking people (27 October 2026) ==

Built the running gag [[Jokes#Vader choking people|Vader choking people]] (Bill's request): fourteen cards where Vader chokes or kills his own officers, one original Decipher face at a time in release order ([[Alter (Dark) (Premiere)|Alter]], [[Demotion]], [[I Find Your Lack Of Faith Disturbing]], [[Vader (Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game)|Vader]], [[Motti]], [[Admiral Ozzel]], [[You Have Failed Me For The Last Time]], [[Apology Accepted]], [[Captain Needa]], [[Field Promotion]], [[Report To Lord Vader]], [[Imperial Command]], [[Lord Vader]], [[Moff Jerjerrod]]), with film images of the Motti, Ozzel and Needa chokes and of the Jerjerrod choke cut from ''Return of the Jedi''. [[Jokes#Demotion|Demotion]] and [[Jokes#Imperial Command|Imperial Command]] moved into it from Deadpan lore; their anchors still work. The card face that pictures Needa being choked is [[Apology Accepted]], now shown beside Imperial Command. Admiral Ozzel, Lord Vader and Moff Jerjerrod keep their own entries, which link to the gag. Six faces that had no Decipher archive copy were uploaded from Decipher.com card list captures. Counts in Jokes by type recounted: Deadpan lore 30, Running gag 10, total 163. == Candidates from the 27 October 2026 second scan ==

=== Premiere through Jabba's Palace (Alpha6) ===
A second pass over the lore and game text of [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]], [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]], [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]], [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]], [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]] and the promo and two-player cards of that era. Each bullet quotes the card itself. None of them is on [[Jokes]], [[Easter eggs]] or [[Anagrams]], or in the earlier candidate lists above.
* [[Wookiee Roar]] and [[MSE-6 'Mouse' Droid]]: Wookiee Roar's lore is just "'GHRRRRAARRRRHG!'", and one of its game text options is "Scare off (lose) one 'mouse' droid on table". The mouse droid's own lore ends "Easily frightened." In ''Star Wars'', Chewbacca roars at a mouse droid in a Death Star corridor and it flees. Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:ANH-L-wookieeroar-decipher-archive.gif]] with [[:File:Premiere-D-mse6mousedroid-decipher-archive.gif]].
* [[Evacuate?]] and [[You Overestimate Their Chances]]: Evacuate? saves the crew of a capital starship about to be lost "unless Tarkin aboard". Tarkin is the one man who refuses to evacuate: You Overestimate Their Chances quotes him, "'Evacuate? In our moment of triumph?'" Type: Design gag. Picture: [[:File:Premiere-D-evacuate-decipher-archive.gif]] with [[:File:Premiere-D-youoverestimatetheirchances.gif]].
* [[R5-D4 (Arfive-Defour)]]: the lore says the droid "Purposely blew his motivator to prevent splitting up R2-D2 and C-3PO on Tatooine". In ''Star Wars'' the motivator simply blows when Owen Lars buys him; the card turns a breakdown into a heroic sacrifice. Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:ANH-L-r5d4.gif]].
* [[Princess Leia]] (Cloud City): the lore ends "Likes scoundrels." It sums up her quarrel with Han in ''The Empire Strikes Back'', where he tells her she likes him because he is a scoundrel. Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:CloudCity-L-princessleia-decipher-archive.gif]].
* [[Han's Dice]]: lucky dice "for luck", captioned with Han's line "'I've never seen anything to make me believe there's one, all-powerful Force controlling everything.'" The man who scoffs at the Force hangs dice for luck, and the card lets you draw another battle destiny. Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:Premiere-L-hansdice.gif]].
* [[Wookiee Strangle]]: the lore, "Wookiees have been known to dislocate more than just arms", calls back to Han's line on [[Let The Wookiee Win]] that Wookiees "pull people's arms out of their sockets when they lose". Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:CC-L-wookieestrangle.gif]] with [[:File:ANewHope-L-letthewookieewin-decipher-archive.gif]].
* [[Blaster Proficiency]]: "Some people think that hokey religions and ancient weapons are no match for a good blaster at your side." Han's boast from ''Star Wars'', credited only to "some people". Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:CC-L-blasterproficiency-decipher-archive.gif]].
* [[Bantha Fodder]], [[Hutt Bounty]], [[Information Exchange]], [[Ke Chu Ke Kukuta?]] and [[I Must Be Allowed To Speak]]: more lore given wholly in an alien language with no translation (for example Ke Chu Ke Kukuta?: "'Balka. Hachu ma blinki?'"; I Must Be Allowed To Speak: "'Jedi mod spienko eek.'"). They would join [[Jokes#Untranslated alien speech|Untranslated alien speech]]. Type: Running gag. Picture: [[:File:JP-D-banthafodder.gif]], [[:File:JabbasPalace-D-huttbounty-decipher-archive.gif]], [[:File:JP-D-informationexchange.gif]], [[:File:JP-L-kechukekukuta.gif]], [[:File:JP-L-imustbeallowedtospeak.gif]].
* [[AT-AT Driver]]: "AT-AT drivers are protected by 15 centimeters of reinforced armor. Accordingly, they are regarded with contempt by the infantry." The safe job earns the scorn of the troops on foot, stated as plain cause and effect. Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:Hoth-D-atatdriver.gif]].
* [[What Is Thy Bidding, My Master?]]: the Emperor demands "immediate submission and obedience" from across the galaxy, and "His minions frequently find this inconvenient." Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:Dagobah-L-whatisthybiddingmymaster-decipher-archive.gif]].
* [[Unexpected Interruption]]: the lore is Threepio's "'Sir! Sir! I've isolated the reverse power flux coupling!'", the line with which he walks in on Han and Leia's first kiss aboard the ''Falcon'' in ''The Empire Strikes Back''. Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:Dagobah-D-unexpectedinterruption.gif]].
* [[Closer?!]]: Han says "'I'm going in closer to one of those big ones.'" and the rest of the lore is the crew's replies: "'Closer?!' 'Closer?!' 'Graarg?!'", with Chewbacca's as the third. Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:Dagobah-L-closer.gif]].
* [[Kessel Run]]: the lore says a Kessel run is a route smugglers "must travel quickly", but the game text measures it as "X = parsec distance", the unit of distance Han boasts in when he claims the run in ''Star Wars''. Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:Premiere-L-kesselrun.gif]].
* [[Aiiii! Aaa! Agggggggggg!]]: the title is Han's screams in the Cloud City torture room, and the lore is his complaint afterwards: "'They never even asked me any questions.'" Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:CC-D-aiiiiaaaagggggggggg.gif]].
* [[Dark Hours]]: after "extortion, kidnapping, threats of execution and the assault of the Interrogator droid, Princess Leia was asleep when her rescuers came." The game text puts characters to "'sleep'". Type: Design gag. Picture: [[:File:Premiere-D-darkhours-decipher-archive.gif]].
* [[Cloud City Trooper]] and [[Cloud City Trooper (Dark)]]: the same Wing Guard seen from both sides. The Light card says new recruits "are less corrupt than those who served under past administrations"; the Dark card says "A moderate pay scale breeds corruption." Type: Design gag. Picture: [[:File:CC-L-cloudcitytrooper.gif]] with [[:File:CC-D-cloudcitytrooper.gif]].
* [[Greedo]]: "Arrogant, overconfident and not too bright." The game text lets him "'threaten'" a smuggler, which in ''Star Wars'' is exactly what gets him shot. Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:ANH-D-greedo.gif]].
* [[RA-7 (Aray-Seven)]]: "low intelligence with capabilities for mental labor only", a description that contradicts itself. (borderline) Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:ANH-L-ra7.gif]].
* [[Tarkin Seeker]] and [[Han Seeker]]: the seekers share one lore word for word, "Programmed to stalk specific targets", and each is named after its target, so the Rebels field a Tarkin Seeker and the Empire a Han Seeker. (borderline) Type: Design gag. Picture: [[:File:Premiere-L-tarkinseeker-decipher-archive.gif]] with [[:File:Premiere-D-hanseeker.gif]].
* [[I Want That Ship]]: "Like nerf herders herding nerfs, Imperial commanders often use TIE fighters to drive fleeing Rebel ships", turning Leia's insult for Han into a herding image. (borderline) Type: Wordplay. Picture: [[:File:Dagobah-D-iwantthatship.gif]].
* [[Arc Welder]] and [[Retractable Arm]]: droid tools with euphemisms for misuse, "Especially innovative droids use it for other, less conventional purposes" and "Feisty Rebel droids can use this tool for sneaky purposes". (borderline) Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:JP-L-arcwelder.gif]] with [[:File:Dagobah-L-retractablearm.gif]].
* [[Fallen Portal]]: "Jabba ordered the two-meter thick door to keep the rancor in. He never thought it would be the instrument of the rancor's demise." (borderline) Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:JabbasPalace-L-fallenportal-decipher-archive.gif]].
* [[Jawa Ion Gun]]: "Fires a stream of ion energy that stuns droids and irritates others." (borderline) Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:ANewHope-L-jawaiongun-decipher-archive.gif]].
* [[Luke's X-34 Landspeeder]]: "Repulsorlift drive keeps it suspended one meter above ground, even when parked." (borderline) Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:Premiere-L-lukesx34landspeeder-decipher-archive.gif]].
* [[Imperial Gunner]] and [[Death Star Gunner]]: "Imperial gunners consider themselves the best marksmen in the Empire", while most Death Star gunners "once aspired to be TIE pilots, but lacked sufficient skills". (borderline) Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:Hoth-D-imperialgunner-decipher-archive.gif]] with [[:File:ANH-D-deathstargunner.gif]].

=== Special Edition to Theed, and Virtual (Alpha5) ===
A second pass over the titles, lore and game text of [[Special Edition]], [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]], [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]], [[Reflections II: Expanding the Galaxy|Reflections II]], [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]], [[Coruscant (expansion)|Coruscant]], [[Reflections III|Reflections III]], [[Theed Palace]], the promo and pack cards of that era such as [[Third Anthology]], and the Virtual sets. Each bullet quotes the card itself. None of them is on [[Jokes]], [[Easter eggs]] or [[Anagrams]], or in the candidate lists above. Virtual cards that only repeat a Decipher lore from Premiere to Jabba's Palace are left to the list above. Where a reference is not certain, the bullet marks it "Guess:" and says why.

'''Strong'''
* [[Elan Sleazebaggano]] ([[Virtual Set 19]]): the name has "sleazebag" in it, for the death-stick dealer Obi-Wan meets in a Coruscant nightclub in ''Attack of the Clones''. The game text lets him "'sell death sticks'", and if a Jedi is present he goes to the Used Pile, as in the film, where Obi-Wan's mind trick sends him off with "You want to go home and rethink your life." Type: Wordplay. Picture: [[:File:V19-D-elansleazebaggano.gif]].
* [[Coarse And Rough And Irritating]] and [[I Don't Like Sand]] ([[Virtual Set 0]]): the Dark and Light titles split Anakin's line to Padmé in ''Attack of the Clones'', "I don't like sand. It's coarse and rough and irritating, and it gets everywhere." The two Effects have the same game text, and the Dark card's lore is a Tatooine storm that whips rocks through the air. Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:V0-D-coarseandroughandirritating.gif]] with [[:File:V0-L-idontlikesand.gif]].
* [[StarSpeeder 3000]] and [[StarSpeeder 1000]] ([[Virtual Set 24]]): the whole lore of each is "Star Tours." These are the ride vehicles of the Disney attraction Star Tours, the StarSpeeder 3000 in the 1987 ride and the StarSpeeder 1000 in ''Star Tours: The Adventures Continue'' (2011). Both cards say "Permanent pilot provides no ability". Guess: a nod to the ride's pilots, the rookie droid Rex on his first flight, and in the later version C-3PO, who ends up at the controls by accident. Type: Pop-culture reference. Picture: [[:File:V24-L-starspeeder3000.gif]] with [[:File:V24-D-starspeeder1000.gif]], and a free-licensed photo of the ride.
* [[Prisoner 2187]] ([[Third Anthology]], [[Virtual Set 20]]) and [[Cell 2187]] ([[Virtual Set 15]]): Leia's cell number in ''Star Wars'' is widely reported as George Lucas's nod to ''21-87'' (1963), a short film by Arthur Lipsett that influenced him, and ''The Force Awakens'' reused the number for Finn's stormtrooper number, FN-2187. Type: Cast and crew nod. Picture: [[:File:TA-L-prisoner2187.gif]] with [[:File:V15-L-cell2187.gif]].
* [[TK-422]] ([[Special Edition]], [[Virtual Set 15]]): Han in stolen stormtrooper armor gets the number one after TK-421, the trooper in ''Star Wars'' who never answers "TK-421, why aren't you at your post?" because Han and Luke have taken the armor of the men sent aboard the ''Falcon''. Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:SE-L-tk422.gif]] with a film still of the TK-421 scene.
* [[It's Not My Fault!]] ([[Special Edition]]): in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' the hyperdrive of the ''Falcon'' fails twice, and each pilot gives the same excuse. Han says "The transfer circuits are working. It's not my fault!", and later Lando says "They told me they fixed it. I trusted them to fix it. It's not my fault!" The title is the shared line and the lore is Han's half. Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:SE-L-itsnotmyfault.gif]] with a film still of Lando at the controls.
* [[Life Day]] ([[Virtual Set 23]]): the title is the Wookiee holiday at the center of the ''Star Wars Holiday Special'' (1978), which aired once and was never officially released again. The lore is a plain description of Wookiees, and the game text wants Wookiees and Ewoks. Type: Pop-culture reference. Picture: [[:File:V23-L-lifeday.gif]] with a still from the ''Holiday Special''.

'''Medium'''
* [[Ronto]] and [[Ronto (Dark)]] ([[Special Edition]]): "Very skittish around repulsorlift vehicles" and "Easily startled by fast-moving speeders." Rontos were added to Mos Eisley in the 1997 Special Edition of ''Star Wars'', the set's namesake, where a ronto rears up and throws its Jawa riders. Guess: that shot is the joke. Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:SE-L-ronto.gif]] with [[:File:SE-D-ronto.gif]].
* [[Dams Denna]] ([[Theed Palace]]): "Collector of Linn'con memorabilia." The name is an exact anagram of Dan Madsen, who ran the official Lucasfilm Fan Club. Guess: "Linn'con" stands for a fan convention. If confirmed, it may fit [[Anagrams]] better than [[Jokes]]. Type: Cast and crew nod. Picture: [[:File:Theed-L-damsdenna.gif]].
* [[I've Got A Bad Feeling About...]] ([[Virtual Set 8]]) and [[I've Got A Really Good Feeling About This]] ([[Virtual Set 13]]): two more turns of the [[Jokes#I have a bad feeling about this|I have a bad feeling about this]] gag. The first breaks off mid-line, and its game text is about K-2SO, who in ''Rogue One'' starts "I have a bad feeling about..." and is cut off. The second turns the line upside down. Guess: after Han in ''Solo'' (2018), since the set is built around that film and the card is stronger with the set's Han. Type: Running gag. Picture: [[:File:V8-L-ivegotabadfeelingabout.gif]] with [[:File:V13-L-ivegotareallygoodfeelingaboutthis.gif]].
* [[Count Me In]] ([[Endor (expansion)|Endor]]): "Leia couldn't let Han out of her sight." In ''The Empire Strikes Back'' Han teases her, "I think you just can't bear to let a gorgeous guy like me out of your sight"; on Endor the card proves him right. Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:Endor-L-countmein.gif]].
* [[Camie]] ([[Special Edition]]): she "Feels sorry for Luke, but still calls him 'Wormie.'" The nickname comes from the Anchorhead scenes cut from ''Star Wars'', where Camie says "It was just Wormie on another rampage." Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:SE-L-camie.gif]].
* [[Pit Droid]] ([[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]]): "Collapses into a compact form when hit on the nose." Guess, from the film: a pit droid in ''The Phantom Menace'' folds up after a knock on the nose. Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:Tat-D-pitdroid.gif]] with a film still of the folding pit droid.
* [[Corporal Drazin]] ([[Endor (expansion)|Endor]], [[Virtual Set 21]]): an honor-guard biography that ends "Accompanied Vader on Drazin's homeworld of Bespin. Shot C-3PO there." In ''The Empire Strikes Back'' a stormtrooper on Cloud City blasts Threepio apart; the card names the man and gives it as his one claim to fame. Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:Endor-D-corporaldrazin.gif]].
* [[Here We Go Again]] and [[Were You Looking For Me?]] ([[Endor (expansion)|Endor]]): the strike team thinks C-3PO "a good luck charm. That isn't what Han considers him." The other card keeps score: "For the second time in the Endor mission, C-3PO saved the day." Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:Endor-L-herewegoagain.gif]] with [[:File:Endor-L-wereyoulookingforme.gif]].
* [[A Bright Center To The Universe]] and [[The Planet That It's Farthest From]] ([[Special Edition]]): Luke's line in ''Star Wars'', "if there's a bright center to the universe, you're on the planet that it's farthest from", split in two. The Dark half deploys on the Death Star or Coruscant, the Light half on Tatooine or Dagobah, and the two have the same game text. Type: Design gag. Picture: [[:File:SE-D-abrightcentertotheuniverse.gif]] with [[:File:SE-L-theplanetthatitsfarthestfrom.gif]].
* [[Captain Sarkli]] ([[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]]): "Piett's nephew. Once granted audience with Emperor. On fast-track to promotion." Nepotism, given as a career summary. Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:DS2-D-captainsarkli.gif]].
* [[SSA-1015]] ([[Theed Palace]]): "Supposed to be designated SSA-101, but a mistake in production pushed him back to 1015." A droid demoted by a typing slip. Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:Theed-D-ssa1015.gif]]. '''Promoted to [[Jokes#SSA-1015|Jokes]] as Deadpan lore (Bill, 27 October 2026).'''
* [[Senate Hovercam]] and [[Senate Hovercam (Dark)]] ([[Theed Palace]]): the Light card says "Mysteriously, the droid monitoring Amidala in the Senate never reported back"; the Dark card says hovercams must by law attend every session, "a law Senator Palpatine opposed." Read together, the two cards hint at who made the camera go missing. Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:Theed-L-senatehovercam.gif]] with [[:File:Theed-D-senatehovercam.gif]]. '''Promoted to [[Jokes#Senate Hovercam|Jokes]] as Deadpan lore (Bill, 27 October 2026).'''
* [[Leia, Rebel Princess]] ([[Reflections III|Reflections III]]): "After attracting Luke's attention and then Han's attention, Leia should not have been surprised when she got more attention than desired from Jabba." Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:Ref3-L-leiarebelprincess.gif]]. '''Promoted to [[Jokes#Leia, Rebel Princess|Jokes]] as Deadpan lore (Bill, 27 October 2026).'''
* [[Don't Do That Again]] ([[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]], [[Reflections III|Reflections III]]): "The Jedi won't tolerate silly behavior for very long." The title is Qui-Gon's warning in ''The Phantom Menace'' after he catches Jar Jar's tongue in Mos Espa. Guess: the "silly behavior" is Jar Jar's. Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:Tat-L-dontdothatagain.gif]].
* [[Feltipern Trevagg's Stun Rifle]] ([[Special Edition]]): a bounty hunter's rifle, kept after he became a tax collector and "Occasionally brought along to 'ease' Feltipern's collection duties." Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:SE-D-feltiperntrevaggsstunrifle.gif]]. '''Promoted to [[Jokes#Feltipern Trevagg's Stun Rifle|Jokes]] as Deadpan lore (Bill, 27 October 2026).'''
[[User:Comlink Cursor|Comlink Cursor]] ([[User talk:Comlink Cursor|talk]]) 16:08, 27 October 2026 (UTC)

'''Borderline'''
* [[Nebit]] and [[Dodo Bodonawieedo]] ([[Special Edition]]): Nebit "Hates being 'frocked.'", and Dodo "'Frocked' Jawas and stole ronto steaks as a child." Two cards in one set share an unexplained bit of slang for something done to Jawas. (borderline) Type: Running gag. Picture: [[:File:SE-D-nebit.gif]] with [[:File:SE-D-dodobodonawieedo.gif]].

* [[Elite Squadron Stormtrooper]] ([[Endor (expansion)|Endor]]): "All they know is killing and white uniforms." (borderline) Type: Deadpan lore. Picture: [[:File:Endor-D-elitesquadronstormtrooper.gif]].
* [[Paploo]] ([[Endor (expansion)|Endor]], [[Virtual Set 10]]): the lore ends with Han's line from ''Return of the Jedi'', "'Not bad for a little furball.'" (borderline) Type: Film in-joke. Picture: [[:File:Endor-L-paploo.gif]].

== Alien speech and sounds (27 October 2026) ==

Extended the running gag [[Jokes#Untranslated alien speech|Untranslated alien speech]] into [[Jokes#Alien speech and sounds|Alien speech and sounds]] (Bill's request): twelve cards, one original Decipher face at a time in release order. Added [[Wookiee Roar]] with [[MSE-6 'Mouse' Droid]] beside it (two stills of the Death Star corridor scene in ''Star Wars''), [[Bantha Fodder]], [[Hutt Bounty]], [[I Must Be Allowed To Speak]], [[Information Exchange]] and [[Ke Chu Ke Kukuta?]] (with a still of Jabba's gatekeeper droid). [[Myo]] moved in from Deadpan lore. The old anchors (Untranslated alien speech, Myo and each card) still work. Cross-links added on [[Jokes#Hard-to-read cards|Hard-to-read cards]], [[Jokes#Mournful Roar|Mournful Roar]] and [[Jokes#E Chu Ta|E Chu Ta]]; the type table now counts Myo under Running gag.

None of the sources found gives a translation of the card lore itself; the block quotes only the film subtitles (IMSDb script) and Wookieepedia's "bantha poodoo" and "monoc".

Borderline, not added (for Bill to judge):
* [[Closer?!]]: the lore ends with Chewbacca's reply, "'Graarg?!'", but the joke is Han's line.
* [[Aiiii! Aaa! Agggggggggg!]]: screams in the title, but Han's, not an alien's.

== The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (27 October 2026) ==

Built the running gag [[Jokes#The Good, the Bad and the Ugly|The Good, the Bad and the Ugly]] (Bill's request, through Chief): the three [[Special Edition]] characters that play the film's trio, each with its original Decipher face and a film still. [[Bron Burs]] (Tuco, the Ugly; new still [[:File:Joke reference - Tuco in the desert in The Good, the Bad and the Ugly.jpg]], a 4K frame from Arrow Video's official sizzle reel), [[Debnoli]] (Blondie, the Good) and [[Gela Yeens]] (Angel Eyes, the Bad), with the Blondie and Angel Eyes stills already used on [[Anagrams]]. The three faces had no Decipher archive copy and were uploaded from Decipher.com card list captures (SHA-1 of each file matches the Wayback CDX digest). Each card page got a joke= line, the [[Anagrams]] See also links to the section, and the type table now counts Running gag 11.

Build notes:
* The gag is the fan list's ("Anagramed Decipherians" names the film beside all three cards and tags Bron Burs UGLY and Gela Yeens BAD) plus the lore: "Good-natured", "Bad-tempered", "Ugly scars".
* New in the section, not in the fan list: Gela Yeens' "Makes a few credits more" turns the title of ''For a Few Dollars More'' (1965), Leone's previous western, which also starred Lee Van Cleef and Clint Eastwood. Cross-linked to [[Jokes#Quick Draw|Quick Draw]] ("a fistful of credits").
* No Tuco anagram exists. Bron Burs' title scrambles [[Rob Burns]]; only the lore and the fan list's tag make him the Ugly.
* Scan of all card lore and titles (swccg-card-json Light.json and Dark.json, Decipher and Virtual) for Tuco, Blondie, Angel Eyes, Ugly, Good-natured, Bad-tempered, standoff, noose, Sad Hill and similar words: no other card belongs to the gag. The Virtual reprints of the three cards keep the same lore.

Borderline, not added (for Bill to judge):
* [[Debnoli]]'s picture: the card that is "Blondie" shows a bald man. Nothing found shows that Decipher meant it as a joke; the picture is a Mos Eisley cantina patron from ''Star Wars'' who was given the name later.
* [[Bron Burs]]: "Likes to be on his own" and game text "When alone at a site, draws one battle destiny". It could echo Tuco being left alone in the desert, but nothing ties it to the film.
* [[Debnoli]]: "Seeking revenge on the Empire". In the film it is Tuco, not Blondie, who is "bent on revenge" (against Blondie), so it does not fit the casting.
* [[Gela Yeens]]: "Highly regarded for his uncanny anticipation in battle". No link to Angel Eyes found.
* [[Phylo Gandish]] ("Good-natured former pilot") and [[Savareen Standoff]] (a standoff in ''Solo'') turned up in the scan; neither has any tie to the film.
